messages:
support_lead: Hey team — drafting the customer-facing maintenance notice + status page blurb for next Tue night change window (UTC 02:00-03:30). Can folks scan for missing risk/rollback bits?

jordan: thanks — quick note: call out which endpoints are impacted (generation vs embeddings) and whether existing keys will be rate-limited during the window.

mike_sre: +1. Also mention pinning behavior: dedicated customers pinned to v1.12 will be unaffected, but hosted traffic may get routed to the fallback model if quantized kernels are upgraded.

support_lead: good point. I'll add a short section: "Who is affected" with exact endpoints.

support_lead: putting draft below — please reply inline with edits.

```STATUSPAGE DRAFT```

We will be performing a maintenance window on Tuesday 2026-05-04 from 02:00 to 03:30 UTC to deploy runtime optimizations and kernel updates. During the window you may see brief increases in request latency and short-lived errors (HTTP 502/504) while connections are migrated. Persistent requests will be retried by our gateway; clients using our SDKs will receive transparent retries for most failures.

Who is affected: Hosted API customers using text-generation and streaming endpoints. Dedicated customers with pinned model versions or private deployments are not expected to be affected unless you use our managed rollout option.

What we're doing: Rolling kernel + quantization pack upgrades to improve tail latency and reduce per-token cost. We'll perform staged canary traffic shifts, followed by cluster-wide rollout.

Risk & rollback: If we observe error rate > 2% or latency > 2x SLO in canaries, we'll halt and rollback to prior kernel build. A full rollback plan is in place and takes ~20-30 minutes to execute.

Customer guidance: No action required. If you rely on strict 99th percentile latency SLAs, consider scheduling high-priority traffic outside the window.

```EMAIL TEMPLATE```

Subject: Planned maintenance — Redwood Inference (May 4, 02:00–03:30 UTC)

Hi there,

We're planning a maintenance window to deploy performance improvements to our inference runtime. You may experience brief increases in latency or short-lived errors during the maintenance window. We have rollback procedures and monitoring in place and will post updates to https://status.redwood.ai.

If you have a Dedicated or Private deployment, this change should not affect you unless you are on managed rollout. Contact your CSM or support if you need an exception.

Thanks,
Redwood Support Team
```

jordan: Looks good. Suggest adding a short "What we tested" line — e.g., canary with 10% traffic for 45m and regression checks vs baseline prompts.

amanda_cs: Can we add customer-facing TL;DR at the top? Something like: "Short: minor performance release — expect minor disruptions, no action required." Customers appreciate that.

support_lead: yes — will add TL;DR.

mike_sre: ops note for internal audience: keep this out of the public docs until we confirm kernel metrics post-canary. Also flag build id and rollback playbook link in internal thread.

support_lead: Roger. I'll publish the public notice once canary reaches 10% with healthy metrics.

deploy-bot: Scheduled change window created: change-20260504-kerner-upgrade (ticket: CHG-4621) — canary at 02:15 UTC.

jordan: can we add a short status page format for automatic ingestion? e.g., one-line summary + impact + updates.

support_lead: added a minimal status summary above. I'll circulate final version in #announcements 24h before.

amanda_cs: I'll prepare a short customer DM template for top 10 enterprise accounts.

mike_sre: And I'll be on-call during the window. If rollback is needed, I'll post timeline and ETA in this thread.

support_lead: thanks all — will update thread with the published status URL and the final email copy tomorrow.
